meta.description: A segmented control of 2, 3 or 4 segments, where the selected segment is filled brand-blue and the others carry a brand-blue outline.

verdict.title: Keep — all four traits pass
verdict.text: Nothing is open. numberOfTabs gives 2, 3 or 4 text segments by design, each filling the width evenly, built from Segmented Control Button instances with every value token-bound.

overview.inContextNote: How the segmented control appears in a real product screen — a two-tab control choosing between Repeat and Schedule Once on Autoload.
overview.livePreviewHtml:
Properties
numberOfTabs

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: numberOfTabs covers 2, 3 and 4 segments, so one component serves every common count.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Owns its own bg / border / label tokens. No external instance dependencies.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: numberOfTabs is a clear, non-positional property. Which segment is active and what each says are set on the segment instances — isActive and the label text.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: Composes Segmented Control Button instances that fill the width evenly, and nests inside Segmented Control - Group as an exposed instance. Segments are text-only by design.

behavior.notes: Pressed state on the tapped segment isn't modeled — should preview the destination on touch-down, commit on touch-up.
Re-tapping the selected segment should be a no-op (or, optionally, reset to a default). Not spec'd.
Each Segmented Control Button carries a Pressed state for the touch-down.
No Focused variant by design — on touch screens the system draws accessibility focus.
Each Segmented Control Button carries a Disabled state.

resolved.body: Component locks 2 segments via positional variants: numberOfTabs now offers 2, 3 and 4 segments — checked on node 26628:50765 (C1)
Positional naming in the selection axis: the selected=first|second axis is gone; each segment carries its own isActive — checked on node 26628:50765 (C2)
Equal-width 168 segments are hardcoded: segments are set to Fill and share the width evenly — checked on node 26628:50765 (C1)

No Focused state: withdrawn — Segmented Control Button ships Default, Pressed and Disabled by design; on touch screens focus is drawn by the system, so no Focused variant is needed — owner decision, 6 Oct 2026, node 26628:50752 (C5)
Segment label is baked text: withdrawn — the label is set by overriding the text on the segment instance, which Figma allows without a property; owner decision, 6 Oct 2026, node 26628:50752 (C4)
No icon or count slot in a segment: withdrawn — segments are text-only by design; owner decision, 6 Oct 2026. Kept as a recommendation for later (C4)

recommendations.headline: Promote to a data-driven EBSegmentedControl.
recommendations.body: Target API: EBSegmentedControl(segments: [Segment], selectedIndex: Int, onChange: (Int) -> Void) where Segment = { id, label, icon?, badge? }. Covers 2-, 3-, 4-segment cases with no per-count variants in Figma.

recommendations.headline: Expose leading-icon + trailing-badge slots per segment.
recommendations.body: Common segmented-control patterns prefix segments with an icon ("⊞ Grid") or append a count badge ("Unread (12)"). Both need named slots so consumers don't detach.

recommendations.headline: Document the A11y model.
recommendations.body: Role: tablist with each segment as tab, currently selected gets aria-selected="true". Keyboard: ←/→ to move, Space/Enter to commit. VoiceOver: "Tab, 1 of 2, selected".

appliedRecommendations.headline: Rename the selected axis to be data-stable.
appliedRecommendations.body: Applied — the positional selected=first|second axis is gone; each segment carries its own isActive (node 26628:50765).

appliedRecommendations.headline: Add Pressed, Focused, and Disabled state coverage.
appliedRecommendations.body: Applied — Pressed and Disabled live in the Segmented Control Button segments; Focused is drawn by the platform, by design (node 26628:50752).

appliedRecommendations.headline: Distribute segment width evenly via flex.
appliedRecommendations.body: Applied — segments are set to Fill and divide the width exactly: 312 ÷ 2, ÷ 3, ÷ 4 (node 26628:50765).

specCards.swift: EBSegmentedControl( segments: ["Label", "Label"], selectedIndex: $selected )
specCards.compose: EBSegmentedControl( segments = listOf("Label", "Label"), selectedIndex = selected, onSelectionChange = { selected = it } )

colorsTables.title: Colors by Segment
colorsTables.description: The control owns one colour — the container border. Everything else belongs to the nested Segmented Control Button (26628:50752) and is identical to the atom. Inactive segments have no fill and no outline — the line you see is a right-edge divider, so it appears only between inactive segments — none at 2 tabs, one at 3, two at 4. The last segment’s divider coincides with the container border and does not render as a second line. Token paths could not be read; the Talk To Figma plugin returns no variable bindings.

Selection and the segment labels have no Figma property behind them: every variant ships the first segment active and every label reading "Label".

accessibility.ios: Each segment is a .button with .isSelected on the active one; the row reads as a single-select set.
accessibility.android: Apply Role.RadioButton per segment inside Modifier.selectableGroup() on the row.

accessibility.ios: Announce position in the set — accessibilityValue of "Label, 1 of 3, selected". The count changes with numberOfTabs, so do not hard-code it.
Segments are 156 / 104 / 78 × 40pt. Every one is under 44pt tall, and at 4 tabs 78pt wide is close to the limit. Extend the hit area with .contentShape; the drawn height belongs to the control.
accessibility.android: Same geometry in dp, all under 48 × 48dp. Use Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize().

accessibility.requirement: Colour is not the only cue
accessibility.ios: Active versus inactive is fill and label colour alone — no icon, no weight change. The .isSelected trait is what carries it for VoiceOver.
accessibility.android: Same. The dividers between inactive segments are decorative and must not be announced.

accessibility.ios: ←/→ should move selection and Space/Enter commit. There is no Focused variant in Figma, so use the platform focus ring rather than inventing one.
accessibility.android: D-pad ←/→ moves selection, Enter commits. Let the platform draw focus; the set has no Focused state to copy.

accessibility.ios: .disabled(true) on the control disables every segment together — there is no per-segment disabled path.
accessibility.android: enabled = false on the row; segments are not individually focusable.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use it for 2 to 4 mutually exclusive views of the same content — a filter across one list, a period switch on one chart.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t use it for navigation between unrelated screens. It is a single-select filter, and the whole row is one control.

usageGuidelines.doText: Keep labels short enough to fit the narrowest segment. At 4 tabs each segment is 78 wide with 16px padding either side, leaving 46 for the text.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t rely on truncation. No variant has a wrap or ellipsis treatment, so an over-long label pushes past its segment.

usageGuidelines.doText: Stay inside 2–4 segments. That is what Figma builds, and the widths divide 312 exactly at each count.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t hand-build a 5-segment control. Nothing in the DS covers it, and the segment width stops being a clean division of 312.

usageGuidelines.doText: Disable the whole control when the choice is unavailable, and set selection from the parent.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t expect Figma to show you a disabled or pressed control. Those states live on the nested Segmented Control Button and are not exposed here — the first segment is active in all three variants.

scorecard.notes: The positional selected=first|second pair is gone and segment widths divide the control exactly — 312 ÷ 2, ÷ 3, ÷ 4. Two to four segments is the intended range — owner decision, 6 Oct 2026; more options call for tabs, chips or a dropdown.
numberOfTabs is a clear, non-positional name with numeric values. It replaced the selected axis, which named a position rather than a property of the control.

Every value is token-bound: the container border border/color-border-primary and radius radius/radius-2; the segments’ fills, strokes, label colours and the Primary/Label/Base text style come bound from Segmented Control Button.
The count maps to a segments array and selection to selectedIndex. Segments are text-only by design; an icon or count slot is a recommendation, not a gap.
The states live in the Segmented Control Button instances — Default, Pressed and Disabled, with isActive per segment — set on each segment, as on the Group.
Text only — no icons or images. If the icon slot in C4 lands, it must accept vector instances.

variants.description: numberOfTabs (3) = 3 variants. The control is 312 × 40 at every count and the segments divide it exactly. The first segment is active in all three; nothing in this set moves the selection. The divider column counts the lines between inactive segments — the boundary beside the active fill needs none, and the last segment’s coincides with the container border.

changelog.header: Rebuilt in Figma on new node 26628:50765

rows.body: The component was rebuilt in Figma and never logged. The record assessed 27:30929; the live set is 26628:50765 and it is named Segmented Control, not Toggle - Segmented Control. Dated when the change was found — nothing records when it was made.

The positional selection axis is gone. selected=first | second — two variants that differed only in which segment was filled — replaced by numberOfTabs (2, 3, 4). The axis now names a property of the control rather than a position within it.

Segment widths now divide the control exactly. The tab documented hardcoded 168-wide segments in a 336-wide control. The control is 312 × 40 and segments are 312 ÷ n — 156, 104, 78. Neither number in the old record was right.

Inactive segments have no fill and no outline. The tab described a white fill with a 1.5px brand-blue outline. There is no fill, and the blue line is a 1px right-edge divider on the segment — which is why it reads as a border only where it meets the container.

Style tab rebuilt to one card with the Figma property panel. A single numberOfTabs control replaces the retired Selected control, which offered First / Second on a set that no longer has a selection axis.

Preview divider bug found and fixed on recheck. The first pass drew a divider on every inactive segment including the last, so it stacked on the container border and the right edge rendered at double weight. Dividers appear only between two inactive segments — none at 2 tabs, one at 3, two at 4. Verified against export_node_as_image and in a browser.
Typography resolved to a style name. Primary/Label/Base, matched, replacing the font spec Proxima Soft Bold · 16 / 16 · +0.25.

Property Mapping rewritten against the current schema. It mapped selected=first / second plus five "(no … today)" rows describing a proposal. Now one prose row per property, with the key distinction stated: numberOfTabs is an enum in Figma and a count in code.
Variants Inventory repointed. Two rows on 27:30930 / 27:30935 at 336 × 40, replaced with three on 26628:50766, 26628:50769, 26628:50773, each carrying its segment width and divider count.
Installation and Usage were empty. Install had planned: true but no blocks, so the badge never rendered; Usage Snippets and Usage Guidelines were both empty. All written, one snippet per tab count.

Accessibility corrected. The tap-target row cited "segments at 168 × 40" and the disabled row invented an opacity 0.4 treatment the component does not use. Rewritten against the real geometry, with a note that the announced count changes with numberOfTabs.
Three tab counts are still three hand-built variants. The data-driven half of the standing recommendation has not landed: a 5-segment control is expressible in code and not in Figma.

The control exposes no State. The nested Segmented Control Button now carries Default, Pressed and Disabled, but none of it is reachable from this set — every variant ships the first segment active, so a pressed or disabled control cannot be drawn.
Still no leading-icon or trailing-badge slot per segment, so the common "filter with counts" pattern cannot be drawn. Unchanged since v1.0.0.
Segment height is under the minimum touch target. 40pt against 44 × 44pt on iOS and 48 × 48dp on Android, and at 4 tabs the 78pt width is close to the limit too.

Divider weight unread. The plugin returns no strokeWeight, and the outside-aligned stroke falls outside the SVG export bounds. Drawn at 1px to match the container border — the one value in the Style tab that is not attested.

Token bindings unread, so all six colour rows carry —. No segmented-control/* namespace is registered; the previous toggle-segmented-control/* paths were not carried forward because they named the retired node.

The Overview tab is entirely pre-rebuild. Zero resolved and six open issues, three of which this rebuild answers — the positional axis, the hardcoded widths, and the name. meta.node still reads 27:30929 and the slug is still toggle-segmented-control. Overview scope.
Component assessed — 2 variants on selected axis. Used in list-view toggles, period pickers, filter chips. Documented
Verdict: Fix — Promote to data-driven EBSegmentedControl with segments array + selectedIndex prop. Add Pressed / Focused / Disabled state coverage. Open
C1 — Hardcoded segment count — Two manual variants lock the count at 2. Replace with segments: [Segment] array. Open
C2 — Positional naming — selected=first|second not stable under reorder. Use selectedIndex: Int. Open
C5 — Missing states — No Pressed, Focused, or Disabled state spec'd. Open
C7 — Code Connect — Not registered. Blocked on restructure. Open
